minutes.headline: Sewer Commission set the new operator contract to start Sept 26, approved connection-policy changes, and tabled the billing tool report.
minutes.summary: The commission met remotely and chose the 26th rather than the 15th as the effective date of the new operations contract. It heard from a BrightFarms civil engineer on the project timeline and Fitchburg flow approval. It tabled the third-party billing tool report until the absent member can review it, approved Article 2 connection policy changes, reviewed invoices and the budget, and named a commissioner to lead the maintenance plan.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved changes to Article 2 (connections and extensions) of the sewer regulations.
The commission tabled the third-party billing tool report until the absent member can review it; it is to lead the next agenda.
A vote set the new operations contract to take effect September 26 rather than September 15; the minutes record the outcome as not audible.
A commissioner was put in charge of the maintenance program, and the maintenance plan is to go on the October 13 agenda.
The commission was told of the BrightFarms connection timeline and Fitchburg flow approval, and the business manager is to keep Fitchburg informed.

why_it_matters: Article 2 sets the rules for connecting to the town sewer, so the approved changes apply to anyone seeking a new connection or extension.
The operations contract date and the billing tool report bear on what the sewer system costs to run and how sewer users are billed, which feeds into sewer rates.
watch_next: October 13 meeting: the maintenance plan is due on the agenda, and the billing tool report is to be first on the next agenda.
October 27 meeting: the new operator is to meet the commission.
